findings.evidence: Radical.lean:26,120,159 puts `Nondegenerate`/`nondegenerate_associated_iff` at `[CommRing R]`+`[Invertible (2:R)]`; Basic.lean:962-971 puts `associated` at `[CommRing R]`; Dual/Lemmas.lean:205-207 gives `forall_dual_apply_eq_zero_iff` at `[Semiring R] [Projective R V]`, and `Fin m → K` is free hence projective by Algebra/Module/Projective.lean:161.
findings.fix: Open a `variable {K : Type*} [CommRing K] [Invertible (2 : K)]` section for the three nondegeneracy declarations (keep `Field` only for `finrank_hyperbolicModel`, `equivalentSumSquares`, `hyperbolicDecomposition`). Two proof adjustments: drop `htwo : (2 : K) ≠ 0` (line 105) and cancel `⅟(2 : K) • _` with `invOf_smul_eq_zero`/`(isUnit_of_invertible 2).smul_eq_zero` instead; and replace the `hsum` argument (lines 124-134), which only works because `Fin (n % 2)` is a subsingleton, with the general `∑ j, z j * Pi.single i 1 j = z i` via `Finset.sum_pi_single'`/`Pi.single_apply` simp.
findings.issue: `hyperbolicModelForm_nondegenerate` (and its helpers `hyperbolicModelForm_associated_apply`, `hyperbolicModelForm_associated_separatingLeft`) pick up `[Field K]` from the line-38 variable block, but nothing in them needs a field: `CommRing K` + `Invertible (2 : K)` suffices. This is stronger than the file's own `hyperbolicModelForm`/`hyperbolicModelForm_apply` (stated at `CommSemiring`, lines 52 and 59) and than the sibling `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Standard.lean:45`, which states its `weightedSumSquares` results at `[CommRing R]`. Roadmap Layers 2-3 (`Suggested.lean:158,166`) work at `[CommRing R] [Invertible (2 : R)]`, so such a consumer can use the model but not its nondegeneracy.

findings.fix: Make it public as `equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isSepClosed` (and, since it is one line away, the two-form corollary `equivalent_of_isSepClosed`, mirroring AlgClosed.lean:61), then derive `hyperbolicDecomposition` from it as the special case it is.
findings.issue: `equivalentSumSquares` is `private`, yet it is strictly more general than Mathlib's public `QuadraticForm.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isAlgClosed` (AlgClosed.lean:51) — same statement with `IsAlgClosed` weakened to `IsSepClosed`, and `IsSepClosed.of_isAlgClosed` (IsSepClosed.lean:70) makes it an actual generalization. The only public classification content is the special case against one fixed model, so a later consumer needing "two nondegenerate forms of equal finrank over a separably closed field are isometric" must re-prove the separable square-root reduction.

summary: The public model-nondegeneracy theorem carries a `Field` assumption it does not use, out of step with the file's own `CommSemiring`-level definitions and the sibling `Standard.lean`. The genuinely general result the file proves — the separably-closed sum-of-squares classification, a strict generalization of two public Mathlib theorems — is hidden behind `private`, leaving only a special case public.
